video_title: Pablo Torre Has a Pulitzer, but Still Feels Like the “Turd” in the Pool | The New Yorker Radio Hour

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The shift from long-form journalism to short-form debate in sports media
quotes.excerpt: the way that people want this is not in the long-form written format that I grew up
quotes.quote: The way that people want this and the way that people are going to want it even more going forward is not in the long-form written format that I grew up fetishizing and learning from and fact-checking, but in argument, in debate, in things that had a clock on screen that said if you don't give a bleep about this topic in less than a minute, we're going to get you to the thing in the short attention span theater of television that you might care about.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Investigating Steve Ballmer's $145 billion investment in the LA Clippers
quotes.excerpt: I did not launch my show to investigate a guy with 145 billion dollars.
quotes.quote: I did not launch my show to investigate a guy with 145 billion dollars. We are talking about Steve Ballmer, the former Microsoft executive and innovator who now owns a professional basketball team, the Los Angeles Clippers. So I got a tip at some point that said, hey, there's a team sponsor with a very on-the-nose brand name called Aspiration, and they are a big sponsor of the Clippers. You should look into them.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The mysterious $7 million debt of Kawhi Leonard's LLC
quotes.excerpt: why is this LLC, if it is in fact Kawhi Leonard's LLC, owed 7 million dollars
quotes.quote: Why is this LLC, if it is in fact Kawhi Leonard's LLC, owed 7 million dollars outstanding by this now-defunct carbon credits company? And you do the thing where you look for every available public record in which there is proof of some business relationship. And there is not. And one of the other things that happens when you are going through the remains of a bankrupt company is that you can start calling people, current and former employees, who now might have insight and more willingness to speak about this.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's secret $50 million payment to Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: Steve Ballmer entered into a secret deal to pay Kawhi Leonard through this company
quotes.quote: According to my reporting, Steve Ballmer entered into a secret deal to pay Kawhi Leonard through this company that he was personally invested in to the tune of 50 million dollars, the biggest investor in the company individually. And Steve Ballmer was, according to my reporting, using Aspiration to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard to circumvent the NBA salary cap.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA salary cap rules and the cost of superstar players
quotes.excerpt: you cannot spend whatever you want to get the thing that in this sport matters the most
quotes.quote: The NBA has some cardinal rules, and one of them, for those not familiar, is that you cannot spend whatever you want to get the thing that in this sport particularly matters the most, which is a superstar player. Five players to a team, that is the fewest of any of the major sports, so a superstar is the thing you need to contend.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Private equity and institutional investors changing NBA team ownership
quotes.excerpt: we are watching the replacement of fans as owners by institutional investors who are here for the growth
quotes.quote: What is happening in sports is that private equity is now being welcomed in. Institutional investors, hedge funds and the like, they are going to be the things that can actually afford these teams. And the reason I spotlight that is because we are watching in sports right now, as the green arrow on sports continues to go up and to the right, we are watching the replacement of fans as owners by institutional investors who are here for the growth, for the profit, for the money.
